title: RNA Guild Kit: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: "I serve only justice. But through that duty, I serve all of Ravnica."
"As peace should be—gentle yet unstoppable." —Augustin IV
"Your potential to commit a crime warrants further investigation."
"Life is fleeting, and so is death. Only the oath is eternal."
As whispers and rumors increased, so did the demand for fail-safe barriers.
"I never thought I'd be so glad to see two tons of beak and claws bearing down on me at the speed of an arrow." —Mirela, Azorius hussar
"It misses nothing and it has no sense of humor." —Barvisa, courtroom scribe
"We have confiscated your spells as evidence. Once we conclude our investigation, you may petition to have them returned."
"Try not to look guilty. Or delicious." —Thorpe, street urchin
"Let the knowledge of absolute law inspire you to live a life of absolute order."
"The higher the mind soars, the greater its understanding of the law." —Isperia
The maze-like design embodies the core of Azorius law—strict structure designed to test wills and stall change.
"Spend your life betraying me if you wish. I'll simply take it up with your ghost."
Rakdos cultists hanged her for sport in the township square. Her ghost now stands vigil at what has become known as the Tree of Weeping.
Her cold wail echoes in the alleys and under-eaves, finding the unfortunate and turning their blood to ice.
"Look at her, once filled with innocence. Death has a way of wringing away such . . . deficiencies." —Savra
"Let him be an example to others who would default on their debts to us." —"The Cozen," Orzhov assassin
"I feel in them a sense of duty and commitment, yet I can feel nothing else. It is as if their duty is to an empty void." —Razia
One moment, conscious only of a sense of repose. The next moment, hearing the trudge of his own footsteps. He sighed and squinted into the glare ahead.
Which is worse—the sleep which never ends or that which never comes?
"That must weigh heavily on your soul. Let me purge it for you."
The form of the sigil is just as important as the sigil itself. If it's carried on a medallion, its bearer is a master. If it's tattooed on the body, its bearer is a slave.
As the bounty on Massacre Girl rose, so did the number of imitators.
"I like a little entertainment with my dinner." —Rakdos
The mask isn't meant to hide his identity. It's meant to keep the viscera out of his eyes.
The fear of dragons is as old and as powerful as the fear of death itself.
"Finally, a weapon the Boros can't confiscate!" —Juri, proprietor of the Juri Revue
Such is the power of Rakdos that even his shadow takes on a cruel life of its own.
Its favorite treats are candied hands and sweet hearts.
In Rakdos-controlled neighborhoods, everyone is part of the show.
Few puppets are so willing.
Sacrificial rites take place before an audience of cheering cultists, each begging to be the next on stage.
Devil-blades and dripping blood make music Rakdos never tires of hearing.
"If there were such a thing as a soul, I think it would be behind the gallbladder but above the kidneys."
When Lord Rakdos stirred from his slumber, everyone else's nightmare began.
Most auramancers would have let the spikes hover just above the skin. Having the spikes rip through the skin from beneath was a touch added by Rakdos himself.
Rakdos festivals almost leave enough rubble in their wake to hide the bodies.
The Rakdos use it for everything you can think of and plenty more than that.
Made of bone and boiled in blood, a Rakdos signet is not considered finished until it has been used as a murder weapon.
Long ago, birds of paradise littered the skies. Thanks to the city's sprawl, most now exist as pets of society's elite.
"Meat *and* eggs. We eat!" —Borborygmos
"The Gruul embrace all things poisonous and living in the cracks of society." —Teysa Karlov
Some use magic to spy through walls. Others use it to crush them.
"It's easy to see why those Gruul dirtbags follow him—the only orders he gives are 'Crush them!' and 'We eat!'" —Teysa Karlov
Those who regard the Gruul as savage simpletons underestimate the subtle power of their shamans.
Gruul shamans are bent on punishing the civilized. Any act more complex than rubbing sticks together or eating with utensils is met with the stinging burn of their magic.
"The Simic come from the cold slow depths. How could they understand the fire in a wild heart?" —Kroshkar, Gruul shaman
"We respect all lifeforms, but this one we respect from a distance." —Mandor, Selesnya ranger
"Not Gruul? Then die!" —Borborygmos
"All the coins in Ravnica can't save his soul now." —Narbulg Nine Fingers
"This city will perish, and the Gruul will cheer as the boar-god crushes the last bricks into dust." —Nikya of the Old Ways
The Orzhov contract the Izzet to animate slum districts and banish them to the wastes. The Gruul adopt them and send them back to the city for vengeance.
"Nature is the ultimate mindless destroyer, capable of power and ferocity no army can match, and the Gruul follow its example." —Trigori, Azorius senator
They inflict pain to forget their own and break foes to feel whole.
"Only the decadent think magic should be pristine and without cost."
Gurley was the first to domesticate one, though his widow didn't take much solace in that accomplishment.
Gruul territorial markings need not be legible. The blood, snot, and muck used to smear them are unmistakably Gruul.
"We've merged your life essence with that of several creatures at once. You're welcome." —Speaker Trifon
"We paid the Simic very well for this capability, but we should quickly recoup our expenses in saved wages." —Milana, Orzhov prelate
It grows to hate you.
Snaking remnants of nature directed by a body of thought and progress, the oracles embody all that is Simic.
"Of course it will grow beyond control—it was designed to choose its own evolution." —Momir Vig
The Simic soon discovered that the sky offered as few constraints on size as the sea.
"This creature has hyperevolved chameleonic abilities. It no longer mimics its surroundings, instead forcing them to take on its form." —Simic research notes
"We've bred out the shortcomings of the species' natural form and replaced them with assets of our own design." —Momir Vig
Held aloft by metabolized magic, trygons are ravenous for sources of mystic fuel.
As the Simic released more of their krasis experiments, they required new habitats, always at the expense of the locals.
"It is technically an ooze, but its life span measures only seconds. In that short time, its appetite for magic is extraordinary." —Simic research notes
"I used to hurl rocks and eat scraps of meat burned over a fire. Look at what I've become and tell me Simic does not hold infinite possibility."

For the Simic Combine, its sigil serves not as an emblem of honor but as a trademark. Its familiar image on any biological commodity attests to superb craftsmanship, ingenious innovation, and higher cost.
